articles.t: Cyberleek publie sa dernière fuite sur GTA 6, renonçant à mettre en ligne une version PC ou des spoilers sur l’histoire
articles.chapeau: Après avoir publié une série de fuites sur GTA 6, Cyberleek affirme avoir mis en ligne ses dernières images. Comme l’objectif en cryptomonnaie n’a pas été atteint, les soutiens ne verront ni révélations sur l’histoire ni version PC jouable. Un extrait de gameplay, censé provenir des dernières missions, commence avec Lucia dans un salon de coiffure.
articles.txt:
Les joueurs inquiets des spoilers sur l’histoire avant la date de sortie de GTA 6 peuvent pousser un soupir de soulagement. Après avoir échoué à atteindre une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars pour un meme coin, Cyberleek affirme avoir publié sa dernière fuite. Les sites de piratage ne verront pas non plus la version PC jouable que Cyberleek menaçait de mettre en ligne. Des séquences centrées sur Lucia , provenant prétendument des dernières missions, accompagnaient le message.
Cyberleek a commencé sa dernière mise à jour en défendant les précédentes ventes massives de cryptomonnaies . Le bourreau de Rockstar soutient que tous les objectifs précédemment atteints ont donné lieu aux fuites de GTA 6 promises. La personne à l’origine des fuites estime avoir été injustement tenue responsable d’une « cascade » de ventes effectuées par d’autres détenteurs.
Les spoilers sur l’histoire sont également exclus, car ils « gâcheraient l’expérience des joueurs, qui n’ont rien fait de mal ». Même si cela porterait gravement préjudice à l’éditeur, Cyberleek déclare : « Take-Two a été suffisamment puni. »
Partager la version PC de plus de 200 Go aurait été encore plus désastreux pour Take-Two et Rockstar Games. Toutefois, sans atteindre l’objectif de 30 millions de dollars en cryptomonnaies, l’individu a estimé que le risque n’en valait pas la peine.
Réaffirmant que les dons étaient une marque de soutien plutôt qu’un investissement, Cyberleek promet que les « fuites s’arrêtent ici. Pour l’instant. » On ignore si Cyberleek refera surface avant la date de sortie de GTA 6 . Quoi qu’il en soit, les fans disposent d’un dernier extrait de gameplay d’environ 4 minutes intitulé « The End of the Road ». "Don't Stop Believin’" de Journey accompagne l’ensemble des images.
Lucia entre d’abord dans un salon de coiffure où des PNJ discutent en arrière-plan. Alors que la partenaire de Jason quitte le commerce, elle frappe le caissier et le dévalise. Une grande partie de la fuite de GTA 6 porte sur des changements de coiffure, puis sur l’achat d’ articles dans une boutique de vêtements.
Les spectateurs ont tout de même un aperçu d’un mini-jeu qui sera disponible. Au cours de ce qui semble être une mission, Lucia joue au billard dans un bar et gagne une petite somme d’argent. Avant la fin de l’extrait, les joueurs découvrent un plan cinématique d’un pont. La vidéo montre différents endroits de Leonida , puis passe à un quartier résidentiel qui semble se trouver dans un autre État que la Floride.

articles.t: GTA 6 : les 200 Go annoncés par Cyberleek ne sont pas la taille du jeu - GinjFo
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek affirme détenir une build de GTA 6 dépassant 200 Go. Ce chiffre lié à une version de développement présumée, ne permet pas d’estimer l’espace nécessaire pour installer le jeu sur PS5 ou Xbox.
articles.txt:
Dans un message du 12 octobre, Cyberleek affirme que la build de GTA 6 qu’il possède dépasse les 200 Go. Une nouvelle fois il menace une diffusion conditionnée à la capitalisation de sa cryptomonnaie.
Il y a cependant un important détail dans ces déclarations. Il s’agit d’un version de développement. Elle peut donc contenir des outils internes, des fichiers temporaires ou des ressources qui ne seront pas intégrées au jeu commercial. Elle peut aussi être moins optimisée. Du coup comparer directement ces 200 Go à la future installation de GTA 6 est trompeur.
Pour le moment Rockstar n’a publié aucune configuration officielle indiquant la place nécessaire sur le SSD d’une PS5 ou d’une Xbox Series X|S. Les 200 Go ne constituent donc ni un prérequis confirmé ni une indication fiable de la taille finale. Les consoles pourraient aussi recevoir des fichiers différents selon la plateforme ou les mises à jour.
La prudence vaut également pour les fichiers présentés en ligne comme une build jouable. Leur origine et leur contenu ne sont pas vérifiés et peuvent s’accompagner de logiciels malveillants et de virus.
L’information la plus utile dans toute cette histoire est que la taille de téléchargement de GTA 6 reste inconnue. Il faudra attendre une annonce de Rockstar ou les fiches officielles des boutiques avant de libérer de l’espace sur sa console.
La sortie du jeu est annoncée sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S le 19 novembre.

articles.t: Cyberleek Returns, Posts More 'GTA VI' Footage, Promises Not to Return Again
articles.chapeau: We can but hope.
articles.txt:
For anyone worried that it’s been several hours since we last heard from valiant pro-physical media warrior and budding crypto entrepreneur Cyberleek , fear not: they’re back. And if you’re wondering whether all the attention of the past few weeks has gone to their alliumal head, consider this: Cyberleek is still referring to themselves in the third person. Readers can draw their own conclusions.
The prolific leaker returned overnight with a new website, a new Grand Theft Auto VI leak, and an update. This, quoth Cyberleek, is the end. If so, they’re going out with a bang: the leak featured footage of the game’s final mission, shorn of context so they wouldn’t risk ruining gamers’ funsies. Cyberleek is also saying that they have footage of the game’s ending, but they’re not going to post it: “[Cyberleek] has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy – why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished.”
Cyberleek: doin’ it for the gamers. Some, however, might suggest that Cyberleek is in fact doing it for the cash. After all, the leaks have coincided with the launch of a memecoin, and all the publicity has driven a whole heap of people toward what would otherwise be just another forgotten slice of the blockchain.
Cyberleek, of course, has no time for such quibblers, calling them godless cynics—or, worse, YouTubers —who don’t understand what Cyberleek is doing for the kids. “The token was only a donation. Never an investment.” Which, I mean, fair: anyone who considers a memecoin linked to an anonymous hacker whose entire public presence involves leaks from a game whose release is a month away an “investment” needs their head examined.
Anyway, it turns out that Cyberleek is disappointed with their flock. The last leak made reference to a secret project for which they were seeking funding: “Cyberleek has a project. Not Rockstar related. Gaming related. It needs expensive hardware. Months to set up. Years to run. Full time.” Well, despite estimates that the coin has allowed Cyberleek to cash out somewhere in the order of $250,000, it seems that this wasn’t enough.
In a sort of pseudo-Kickstarter structure, Cyberleek tied various milestones to the memecoin’s market capitalization, including a release of the entire game if the market cap hit $30m. It… did not. At all. The coin’s market cap is currently sitting at around $1m, which just goes to show that there are only so many people with Pepe avatars you can fleece at any given moment.
But Cyberleek isn’t mad; they’re just disappointed: “The [milestone] was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written. Sad.” That’s right: no game for you, and it’s your own fault. I hope you’re happy.
As ever, it’s not clear whether Cyberleek is one person, multiple people, or a state of mind, but the prose in last night’s announcement certainly matched the sort of sub-LinkedIn style of previous posts, with its heavy use of the passive voice and strange, stop-start sentence structure, so it seems reasonable to assume that whoever was behind the previous leaks was also behind this one. Is this the last we’ll hear from them? With over a month until GTA VI launches, that feels unlikely, but we’ll see.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' file size: Cyberleek reveals eye-watering storage requirements
articles.chapeau: Take it with a grain of salt, of course.
articles.txt:
The person leaking a bunch of gameplay videos of Grand Theft Auto VI may have just revealed the most useful information in all of their leaks.
On the Cyberleek website (per our colleagues at PCMag ), one of the latest updates included a threat to release a full build of the game in some form if people on the internet raised the leaker's crypto memecoin to a $30 million market cap. The coin has since crashed and looks like it's not going to get anywhere close to that level, but more importantly, the update included a file size for the playable build they have evidently been taking clips from: 200GB.
That's obviously a huge number, and makes up more than 20 percent of the usable storage space on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X console. Perhaps surprisingly, it's not as big as some other games, as recent Call of Duty titles clear 200GB by a good margin. But it would still be one of the biggest single-player file sizes we've seen yet, and speaks to the scale and scope of GTA 6 .
Of course, this should be taken with at least a tiny bit of skepticism. We don't know much about the build Cyberleek has been leaking footage from. If they do indeed have the full game on hand, it could be an older build that hasn't been fully optimized yet, so the true GTA 6 file size could theoretically be smaller once the actual game comes out on Nov. 19.

The game is still scheduled for November 19. Chris Bratt of People Make Games says a tribunal between Rockstar and 34 fired workers will meet on November 17 and 18.
Some X users speculate that the fired employees may include Cyberleek, though nothing confirms the idea. The clips, however, are shown without context, which makes their authenticity hard to verify.
The leaker releases unreleased GTA 6 material and ties each new drop to the market value of the CYBERLEEK token. In effect, its price decides how much of the game reaches fans.
CYBERLEEK fell 41% in 24 hours and trades near $0.00155, according to CoinGecko data. That price sits roughly 96% below its all-time high.
Valuation milestones have shaped every release since the start. The first leaks pushed the token to a $40 million market cap.
The token then climbed 200% in two days, yet it still fell short of that earlier peak. Cyberleek responded by withholding the full build. Its market cap sits a little above $1 million, far below the $30 million target.
The roadmap ties future drops to milestones of several million dollars in market cap. Regular releases will stop, the leaker says, because the token is performing poorly.

articles.t: GTA 6 Cyberleek update: Leaker linked GTA 6 reveals to crypto play. It’s crashing spectacularly.
articles.chapeau: The Cyberleek memecoin is now plunging further and further.
articles.txt:
As Mashable and our colleagues at PCMag just reported, Grand Theft Auto VI leakers Cyberleek have seemingly abandoned their threats to leak a full build of the game – at least for now.
Why? Because the leakers had claimed that the release of the leaked build was tied to their memecoin. If GTA 6 fans pumped Cyberleek's cryptocurrency, they would receive the leaked game build as a reward.
That play failed spectacularly for Cyberleek. In fact, it seems to have fully backfired.
The Cyberleek memecoin's market cap hit a high of $7.8 million on October 11, shortly after the leakers claimed they would release the full build of GTA 6 supposedly in their possession. The catch? The Cyberleek memecoin had to hit a market cap of $30 million first. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile
While some GTA 6 fans appeared to have bought into the memecoin in an attempt to hit Cyberleek's goal, $7.8 million is still far short of the $30 million the leakers wanted. And since then, as it became obvious that most GTA 6 fans weren't going to give in to Cyberleek's demands, the memecoin has plunged even further, with a current market cap of $1.17 million.
Critics of Cyberleek celebrated the memecoin's failure, calling it a scam.
Cyberleek had been successful with their memecoin play before, giving those who bought their memecoin exclusive access to polls that determined what GTA 6 footage the leakers would release next.
However, it seems Cyberleek overplayed their hand this time around, and the full build, which they claim is 200GB, appears to be staying under wraps for now.
With that said, Cyberleek is still using their supposed access to a full build of GTA 6 to try to escape legal action from Take-Two, the parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games. The leakers claim that there is a "dead-man's switch" that will automatically release the ending of the game if there is an attempt to take down Cyberleek.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' Cyberleek release updates: What leaked, what's next
articles.chapeau: Maybe don't watch these videos on your work device.
articles.txt:
If you simply can't get enough of Grand Theft Auto VI prior to its Nov. 19 release, there are still new GTA 6 leaks coming out.
Cyberleek , the anonymous entity that has been leaking clips from a pre-release build of GTA 6 since August, made their grand return in October after about a month of silence. Last week, Cyberleek posted a 24-minute video that seemed to show some story sequences and a glimpse of the male protagonist Jason rendered completely nude. That wasn't the end of it.
And, as Cyberleek said they would, nude clips of the female protagonist Lucia soon followed. On top of that, Cyberleek is now threatening to release a development build of the game, and according to Dextero, may have already done so . Websites affiliated with Cyberleek include a link to a file named GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1, locked behind a $40 paywall.
It should go without saying that downloading files from a sketchy website is not a wise idea, nor is purchasing illegal content that violates Rockstar's copyright.
Cyberleek returned this week with more clips that you definitely should not watch at work.
That's because these new clips all center on the female protagonist, Lucia, nude. In the clips, Lucia does mundane things like walk around Vice City, drive a vehicle, and parachute off a skyscraper while wearing little to no clothes (OK, so not entirely mundane, actually). It doesn't seem like anything new has been posted since Monday morning, though.
One thing to note about these clips: The nudity doesn't appear to be a normal element of the gameplay, but rather some type of mod. Rockstar has designed its last couple of big open-world adventures around extremely reactive NPCs, and none of them react at all to seeing Jason or Lucia nude in these leaked clips. Between that, and another clip from last week where the player spawns a tank out of thin air, it sure seems like developer tools are being used to achieve outcomes that will not be possible in the final game.
In other words, don't expect to be able to streak around Vice City in the nude on Nov. 19.
On websites associated with Cyberleek, the leaker threatened to release a full playthrough of the entire GTA 6 story if their memecoin reached $30 million in market value. The leaker also threatened to release a development build of the game if Rockstar failed to meet their demands to release GTA 6 on a physical disc. There's just one problem: The coin is tanking.
IGN reported a market cap of just $1.7 million, well below any of the stretch goals specified by Cyberleek, and certainly not even close to the $7.8 million high it reached on Oct. 11. Despite this, Cyberleek may have made good on their threat to release a development build of the game.
Dextero is reporting that the development build has been posted online, locked behind a $40 paywall. In addition, a Cyberleek website with all of the leaked clips now includes this update, posted on Oct. 13: " DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT: GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025 is up. The deal was 30 million marketcap and the build goes out. Cap was not hit. Build is out anyway. $40 per download. Pay it, then take the mirror."
Because the leaker is anonymous, and because it would be illegal and dangerous to download mystery files from an unverified website, we can't confirm that this development build is real, or that it was even directly posted by Cyberleek.
However, if there is now a development build floating around the web, expect to see far more GTA 6 leaks in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 19 release date.
Alternatively, you could wait and play the game when it actually comes out. You can preorder the game now .
A Cyberleek website includes a poll about what type of Lucia content to release next. The poll is set to end on Oct. 14, with the leading option as "Race track."
It seems extremely likely that more clips featuring Lucia are set to be released any day now.

articles.chapeau: CyberLeek affirme qu’une build de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go sur PS5 et Xbox Series, faisant grimper la pression avant novembre 2026. Jusqu’où ce fichier pourrait-il bousculer votre stockage ?
articles.txt:
CyberLeek affirme qu’une build de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go sur PS5 et Xbox Series, faisant grimper la pression avant novembre 2026. Jusqu’où ce fichier pourrait-il bousculer votre stockage ?
Le prochain monstre de Rockstar Games ne sera pas seulement gigantesque sur la carte. Selon le leaker CyberLeek , une build jouable de GTA 6 dépasserait les 200 Go , de quoi affoler les possesseurs de PS5 et de Xbox Series X|S déjà à court de SSD.
Au 13 octobre 2026, la taille de fichier officielle de GTA 6 n’apparaît toujours pas sur le PlayStation Store ni sur le Xbox Store, mais la sortie console est bien fixée au 19 novembre 2026, avec préchargement dès le 12 novembre. Alors, combien de Go faudra-t-il vraiment libérer sur votre console ?
CyberLeek affirme qu’un build complet et jouable de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go. D’après Notebookcheck, ce chiffre vient d’une version de développement interne, utilisée pour les tests et les vidéos leakées, et reprise par des comptes spécialisés comme GTA 6 Info sur X.
Il faut surtout comprendre qu’une build de développement ne correspond pas à la taille d’installation finale. Elle embarque des outils, des données de test et des assets en doublon. Notebookcheck rappelle qu’une archive de développement de GTA 5 avait déjà atteint 192 Go alors que le jeu pèse environ 95 Go sur PS5 et 105 Go sur PC.
Le monde ouvert de GTA 6 , situé à Leonida autour de Vice City, est annoncé comme environ deux fois plus vaste que celui de GTA 5 , avec beaucoup plus de détails. Logiquement, la taille de téléchargement sera nettement supérieure aux 95 Go actuels du précédent opus sur PS5.
Certains Call of Duty: Black Ops dépassent déjà les 200 Go, prouvant qu’un AAA console peut atteindre ce palier. La plupart des estimations sérieuses situent toutefois la taille d’installation de GTA 6 dans une fourchette de 150 à 200 Go. Les 200+ Go évoqués par CyberLeek semblent représenter la borne haute, pas forcément le poids exact sur PS5 ou Xbox Series X|S.
Sur une PS5 , le SSD de 825 Go laisse bien moins d’espace réellement disponible une fois le système installé. Un fichier de 180 à 200 Go pour GTA 6 pourrait occuper près d’un quart du stockage, surtout problématique sur PS5 Digital. Même constat sur Xbox Series S , dont le SSD de 512 Go est vite saturé.
Notebookcheck souligne que l’extension de stockage sur PS5 et Xbox est devenue coûteuse avec la hausse des prix des composants. Entre SSD M.2 certifiés pour PS5 et cartes d’extension propriétaires pour Xbox, il faudra peut-être choisir entre investir ou désinstaller plusieurs AAA pour faire de la place.
Autre contrainte, les joueurs soumis à une limite de données internet mensuelle. Sans disque complet en Blu-ray et avec des versions souvent réduites à un code de téléchargement, un éventuel téléchargement de 150 à 200 Go pèsera lourd sur le forfait, surtout si des mises à jour massives suivent le lancement.
La bonne nouvelle, c’est que Rockstar a prévu un préchargement dès le 12 novembre 2026. Vous aurez une semaine pour libérer de l’espace, lancer le téléchargement en heures creuses et éviter de saturer votre connexion avant de plonger dans Leonida le 19 novembre.
